# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

The fix is complete. Here's what I changed in `textkit/slug.py`:

1. **Collapse consecutive non-alphanumeric characters**: Changed the regex from `r"[^a-z0-9]"` to `r"[^a-z0-9]+"`. The `+` quantifier matches one or more consecutive non-alphanumeric characters and replaces them with a single hyphen, fixing the double-hyphen issue (e.g., `"Hello,  World!"` → `"hello-world"` instead of `"hello--world-"`).

2. **Strip leading/trailing hyphens**: Added `text = text.strip("-")` to remove any hyphens at the beginning or end of the string, fixing the trailing hyphen issue (e.g., `"--a--b--"` → `"a-b"`).

All existing tests pass.

arguments.summary: Fixed `slugify` in `textkit/slug.py` by (1) changing the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` to collapse consecutive non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen, and (2) adding `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This resolves the double-hyphen and trailing-hyphen issues described in the issue.
